**Reasoning**

Electrical conductivity depends on how easily charge carriers (electrons or ions) can move through a material.

| Material | Typical charge carriers | Conductivity (relative) | Comments |
|----------|------------------------|--------------------------|----------|
| **Aluminum** | Free electrons (metal) | High | Good conductor, used for power lines. |
| **Copper** | Free electrons (metal) | Very high (higher than Al) | One of the best conductors, standard wiring material. |
| **Plastic** | No free electrons or ions (polymer) | Extremely low | An electrical **insulator**; used to coat wires. |
| **Water** | Ions (from dissolved salts, minerals) | Low‑to‑moderate | Pure water is a poor conductor, but ordinary water contains enough ions to conduct noticeably. It conducts better than an insulating polymer. |

Comparing the four, the two metals conduct best, water conducts modestly (especially when it contains impurities), and plastic conducts virtually none. Therefore, plastic is the material **least likely** to allow electricity to flow.

**Conclusion**

The correct choice is **C**.

**Final answer:** C
